beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The people Paul was writing to had once been outsiders — foreigners, strangers, on the far edge of God's promises, with no place at the table and no share in the family.

timing.text: The people Paul was writing to had once been outsiders — foreigners, strangers, on the far edge of God's promises, with no place at the table and no share in the family.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: But something had changed everything. The door had been thrown open, and those who were far off had been brought near — no longer guests to be tolerated, but family to be embraced.

timing.text: But something had changed everything.
The door had been thrown open, and those who were far off had been brought near — no longer guests to be tolerated, but family to be embraced.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Paul reached for a beautiful picture: Not a crowd of strangers passing through, but sons and daughters at home, belonging.

timing.text: Paul reached for a beautiful picture: Not a crowd of strangers passing through, but sons and daughters at home, belonging.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;

timing.text: Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: But a household needs a house — and a house needs to be built, and built right. So Paul changed the picture from a family to a building, the dwelling place of God among his people.

timing.text: But a household needs a house — and a house needs to be built, and built right.
So Paul changed the picture from a family to a building, the dwelling place of God among his people.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Every real building rests on a foundation. And this one, Paul said, was laid on the apostles and the prophets — men God had called and taught, whose witness became the solid ground the whole structure would stand on.

timing.text: Every real building rests on a foundation.
And this one, Paul said, was laid on the apostles and the prophets — men God had called and taught, whose witness became the solid ground the whole structure would stand on.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And at the most important place of all — the cornerstone, the stone that sets the angle, holds two walls together, and keeps the whole building square and true — stood Christ himself. Everything is lined up to him.

timing.text: And at the most important place of all — the cornerstone, the stone that sets the angle, holds two walls together, and keeps the whole building square and true — stood Christ himself.
Everything is lined up to him.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone;

timing.text: And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone;

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So the church was never meant to be a loose, shapeless crowd. It has a design — a foundation of apostles and prophets, a cornerstone that is Christ, and living people fitted together into a home for God. There is a blueprint.

timing.text: So the church was never meant to be a loose, shapeless crowd.
It has a design — a foundation of apostles and prophets, a cornerstone that is Christ, and living people fitted together into a home for God.
There is a blueprint.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And the best part is where that leaves you. You are not a stranger at the door. In this house you have a place, fitted in and belonging, part of what God is building. So the only question is a hopeful one. When he offers you a place in it, will you come inside?

card.text: You are no longer a stranger, but part of the household of God — a building laid on apostles and prophets, with Christ the cornerstone holding it all together. When he offers you a place in it, will you come inside?
